name: REVERSIS
description: Reversis is an ancestor of Hearts from around 1600, popular in the 17th and 18th centuries. Trick avoidance: avoid taking penalty cards (hearts, queen of spades). David Parlett documents rules and history.

content.text: Reversis is an ancestor of Hearts from around 1600, popular in the 17th and 18th centuries. Trick avoidance: avoid taking penalty cards (hearts, queen of spades). David Parlett documents rules and history.

Reversis was first documented in France in 1601 under the name Reversin, played with a 52-card pack and celebrated in a poem by Antoine du Brueil around 1611. Its origin is uncertain but may have emerged in Italy before spreading to Spain and France. It is one of two probable ancestors of Hearts and Black Maria, the other being Coquimbert. The game was very popular with the French aristocracy in the 17th and 18th centuries and was much played elsewhere except in Britain. Jean-Baptiste Bullet suggested it was invented at the Court of Francis I. Spaniards called it La Gana pierde (the winner loses) because in Reversis the lowest cards had preference—the Jack outranked the King—inverting normal play.
Standard 52-card French-suited pack; later rule sets use 48 cards with tens removed. Thirteen cards per player for four players. No trumps; cards rank A K Q J down to 2.
